w: Swamishri performed the murti pratishtha ceremony at the Shree Swaminarayan Mandir, Jersey city. More than 470 devotees had participated in the Vedic ceremony.
Swamishri performed the foundation-stone laying ceremony for a Hari mandir in Gandhidham. Thereafter, Swamishri performed the murti-pratishtha ceremony of deities in a temporary Hari mandir.
Swamishri's Shri Harikrishna Maharaj (Thakorji) was honored by the devotees. Finally Swamishri blessed the assembly.
In the evening, Swamishri returned to Bhuj and addressed the satsang assembly.

Today the murtis of guru parampara and Radha-Krishna dev, Sita-Ram dev, etc. The preliminary rituals began in the presence of Mahant Swami, Dr Swami and Kothari Swami. Swamishri arrived earlier than scheduled. Amidst Vedic chantings Swamishri placed the Yantra, Kurma and Anant devas inside the base on which the murtis would rest. Thereafter Swamishri, senior sadhus and devotees performed arti and mantra pushpanjali. Then Swamishri went to place the Yantra in the base of the Sanatan devas. After placing the Yantra and Anant in the base where Sita-Ram dev were to be installed, Swamishri was about to place the Kurma dev when an earthquake shook the monument. It was 9.27 am. Immediately Swamishri was led outside and all the sadhus and devotees gathered outside by the steps of Akshardham. The epicenter of the 7.6 Richter scale earthquake was near Islamabad in Pakistan. Thereafter Swamishri chanted the Swaminarayan dhun for things to return to normal. After the dhun Swamishri said, “By the grace of Bhagwan Swaminarayan everything has become quiet and calm. Any obstacle that is destined for the future has come in a little way today. Now it has quietened down. Shesh Narayan has been installed. Now, all obstacles have gone. What was to come later has come before. A greater calamity has been resolved into a minor disturbance. Now, no more problems will arise and everything will turn out well.”
At 6.00 pm Swamishri inaugurated the large format film theater called Neelkanth Darshan. Thereafter Swamishri and the sadhus saw the film on Neelkanth Varni.

st.t: A Spiritual Travelogue of Pramukh Swami Maharaj - New Delhi Page-1, 8 October 2005
w: Pindika Pujan (Pujan of murtis' Seat) A ritual pujan of the seat of the murtis of Guru Parampara and deities of Sanatan Dharma was performed in the morning in Akshardham monument. Prior to the rituals, Pramukh Swami Maharaj performed the pujan of the gold yantras and silver forms of sheshnag, kurma, etc. which symbolize the forces of nature to be placed in the hollows of the seat of the murtis of Guru Parampara. Thereafter Swamishri and senior sadhus arrived at the monument for the Pindika pujan. After the Pindika pujan for the murtis of Sita-Ram, Radha-Krishna, etc. an earthquake took place. Swamishri and all sadhus and devotees chanted dhun outside the Akshardham monument.

The National Sanyukta Mandal Shibir, attended by over 1,500 devotees from the ages of 40 to 95 was held in the presence of Pramukh Swami Maharaj at the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London. Entitled ‘Shatabdi Yatra’, the shibir highlighted the hundred-year journey of BAPS from its difficult beginnings with Shastriji Maharaj, to its nourishment from Yogiji Maharaj, and worldwide advancement by Pramukh Swami Maharaj. The first session focused on Shastriji Maharaj, wherein the opening speech by Viveksagar Swami related about the firm resolve of the founder of BAPS. After an enlivening kirtan, Anandswarup Swami spoke about the virtues and personality of Shastriji Maharaj. The afternoon session centred around the persona of Yogiji Maharaj, introduced through a video presentation, and elaborated in greater detail in a speech by Ishwarcharan Swami. A video on Yogiji Maharaj provided touching memories to conclude the session. In the evening session, Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s life and work were narrated by Anandswarup Swami. Thereafter Gnaneshwar Swami explained the necessity of Niyam-Dharma. Viveksagar Swami enlightened everyone on their personal responsibilities for the centenary year of BAPS, explaining how each individual can contribute to the Sanstha’s progress. Continuing on the theme of personal progresss, a series of short skits, entitled Satsangi to tene re kahiye, inspired the devotees to strengthen their fundamental practices as a satsangi. Swamishri then blessed the shibir, emphasizing the importance of observing the basic niyams prescribed by Bhagwan Swaminarayan, and also providing practical solutions to avoid any slackness in moral observances.

st.t: BAPS News – National Sanyukta Mandal Shibir 2007 – Monday 8 October 2007
w: The National Sanyukta Mandal Shibir, attended by over 1,500 delegates, was held in the presence of Pramukh Swami Maharaj on Monday 8 October 2007 at BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Mandir, London. Entitled ‘Shatabdi Yatra’, the shibir highlighted the hundred-year journey of BAPS from its arduous beginnings with Shastriji Maharaj, to its nourishment from Yogiji Maharaj, and worldwide advancement by Pramukh Swami Maharaj.

The first session focused on Shastriji Maharaj, wherein the opening speech by Viveksagar Swami discussed the firm resolve of the founder of BAPS. After an enlivening kirtan, Anandswarup Swami spoke of the virtues and personality of Shastriji Maharaj, providing an entertaining and informative discussion.

The afternoon session centred around the persona of Yogiji Maharaj, introduced through a video presentation, and elaborated in greater detail by Ishwarcharan Swami. A further video provided touching memories to conclude the session.

Pramukh Swami Maharaj’s life and work were narrated by Anandswarup Swami, before a speech by Gnaneshwar Swami on the subject of niyam-dharma. Viveksagar Swami enlightened everyone on their personal responsibilities for this centenary year of BAPS, explaining how each individual can contribute to the Sanstha’s work. Continuing on the theme of personal progression, a series of short sketches, entitled ‘Satsangi To Tene Re Kahiye’ , inspired the delegates to strengthen their fundamental practices as a satsangi.

Swamishri then blessed this final session of the shibir, emphasising the importance of observing the basic niyams prescribed by Bhagwan Swaminarayan, and also providing a practical solution to avoid any slackness in these observances.

At the age of 87 years Swamishri personally wished to perform the foundation-stone laying ceremony for the grand shikharbaddh Swaminarayan mandir in Jamnagar. The Vedic rituals commenced at 7.00 a.m. The entire walls of the foundation pit were adorned with red plastic and saris. A small canopy was set up over the main platform for the ritual ceremony. In all, there were 27 main shilas. Around each of the shilas Tyagvallabh Swami, Viveksagar Swami, Kothari Jnanprasad Swami and other sadhus, guests and devotees performed the rituals. Thousands of devotees also performed the rituals with each having a foundation brick before them. When Swamishri arrived he performed the foundation-stone laying rituals from the main stage. More than 7,500 devotees participated in the rituals. After completing the rituals an assembly was held. The invited guests who honoured Swamishri were Mayor Kanaksinh Jadeja, Retired Air Marshall Mehra, MLA Mulubhai Bera, MLA Laljibhai Solanki, Collector V.P. Patel, City Commissioner K.N. Bhatt, IGP Shri Rabari, DSP Shri Jotangiya, Air Force Head Shri Harikumar and district president of BJP Shri Narendrabhai Trivedi. The former Defence Minister of India, Shri George Fernandes, sent a goodwill message for the occasion and regretted for being unable to attend the function due to ill health. His message was read out in the assembly, “Unfortunately, I will not be able to be physically present, but shall be very much there in mind and spirit. This is because I deeply value and appreciate the great work of national pride, goodness and unity that HDH Pramukh Swami Maharaj is doing through the many BAPS services of health, education, culture and character throughout the world. Also, amazing cultural centres like Swaminarayan Akshardham in Delhi and Gandhinagar have become places of great inspiration and integration. But most importantly, I value the humility and simplicity of Swamiji, whom I have met a few times, and whose presence has filled me with utter calm and spiritual peace. Today, I extend my full support to the new complex at Jamnagar and the values upheld by BAPS… I salute all ideals and institutions that work for unity, peace and progress of our people and our nation and BAPS is one that I personally respect and revere. May the centre at Jamnagar help elevate society in the right moral, ethical and spiritual direction which remains the urgent need of our times.” Collector Shri V.P. Patel said, “The BAPS Swaminarayan mandirs are centres of culture and character-building. Primarily they inculcate values among the young.”

Commissioner Shri K.N. Bhatt expressed his feelings, “Only through God’s grace can a mandir be built here. Pramukh Swami’s uniqueness is that no matter how great his works, he is simple, humble, polite and determined.” Mayor Shri Kanaksinh Jadeja said, “A golden sun has dawned in the form of Pramukh Swami in Jamnagar today. An edifice to build character is going to be constructed here.”

Finally, the assembly climaxed with Swamishri’s blessings, “The foundation-stone laying ceremony has been performed in the presence of God, officers, everyone and especially Marshall Saheb. The foundation rituals were completed nicely through the cooperation of officials, devotees, businessmen and everyone. The crux of the matter is that we should never forget God who has given us this life. He has given us this life so that we may do good works, serve the nation and society. People in our country have a lot of spiritual faith. There are thousands of mandirs in which devotees worship God according to their means and faith. Yogiji Maharaj used to say, ‘May God do good of all.’ God has given us this human body so that we can do our social duties, and offer service to the nation and God. Together with this we must also strive for self-elevation.” The assembly concluded at 11.07 a.m. About 12,000 devotees were served mahaprasad.
Jamnagar has been known since ancient times as Little Kashi, and sanctified on numerous occasions by Bhagwan Swaminarayan and the parmahansas of the Swaminarayan Sampraday.
There, on Wednesday 8 October 2008, the auspicious Shilanyas Ceremony for a new BAPS shikharbaddh mandir was performed by Pramukh Swami Maharaj.

Over 8,500 devotees participated as yajmans in the mahapuja from 7.00 to 9.00 am. Thereafter Swamishri performed pujan and arti of the shilas (stones) and then placed the sanctified shilas and the auspicious nidhi-kumbh in the foundations.

Among the dignitaries present were Air Marshall Mehra, former Air Marshall of the Western Air Command; Mayor Shri Kanaksinhji Jadeja; Shri Mulubhai Bera, MLA; Shri Laljibhai Solanki, MLA; Shri V.P. Patel, Collector, and others.

A letter of good wishes from India's former Defence Minister, Shri George Fernandes, was read. Addressing the gathering, Air Marshall Mehra said, "Just as soldiers ignore all barriers of faith and communities to help everyone in need, the sadhus and volunteers of BAPS are also working for the good of all humanity."
Finally, Swamishri blessed the 12,000 devotees gathered for this auspicious occasion. After the assembly, all yajmans entered the foundation to place a brick and took mahaprasad.

Today Pramukh Swami Maharaj was to leave from here for Junagadh. In this context, Nilkanthseva Swami, sitting in the Rupchoki, said, "You are going from here to Junagadh. Will it suit you there? The water there is hard and stony."

In a mood of joy, Swamishri said, "Why! Gunatitanand Swami lived there, Shriji Maharaj also went there, and it is the land of Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj. If they could digest the stony water, can we not digest it?"
Pramukh Swami Maharaj came for the darshan of Hanumanji and Ganpatiji. Here Brahmasetu Swami recited a line, "I remember the divine episodes...."
Swamishri said, "That is right. If it comes into our heart, then there is peace, peace."

Today Pramukh Swami Maharaj was to go from here to Junagadh. In this connection, Nilkanthseva Swami, sitting in the Rupchoki, said, "You are going from here to Junagadh, will it suit you there? The water there is stony."

In high spirits, Swamishri said, "Oh! Gunatitanand Swami lived there, Shriji Maharaj too went there, it is the land of Shastriji Maharaj and Yogiji Maharaj. If they digested the stony water, can we not digest it?"
Pramukh Swami Maharaj came for the darshan of Hanumanji and Ganpatiji. Here Brahmasetu Swami sang a line, "I remember his divine actions and incidents..."
Swamishri said, "That is right. If it enters the heart, then there is peace, peace."

ds.t: Remembering Maharaj and Swami is rest
w: Today after the mangala arti, Mahant Swami Maharaj lay down on his bed for a short rest. But within just ten minutes he got up. Seeing this, the sadhus asked, "Couldn't you sleep? Don't you want to rest?"
"What rest! Remembering Maharaj and Swami, that itself is rest," Swamishri said in the carefree joy of devotion.
"Hearing and reflecting on my virtues in his heart..." This is the abiding feeling of Swamishri's life.
After having darshan upstairs in the mandir, on coming to the lift, Mahant Swami Maharaj asked, "Is Sitaji's sari pink?"
The sadhus coming behind looked and said, "No, Swami! It is lemon yellow." Saying "Yes", Swamishri entered the lift.
A thought came to the attendant sadhu and he asked, "Swami! Why did you ask that? Do you remember all the vaghas (garments of the murtis) every day?"
Swamishri replied, "I do not have to remember. It comes to mind naturally... Whatever darshan I have had comes to mind naturally while leaving."
Usually, while leaving after darshan, Swamishri meets the devotees through his gaze. But today we learned that at that very time he is also remembering the murti.

Mahant Swami Maharaj arrived at the Chigwell mandir. The annakut (offering of many foods) had been arranged here. The arti had already been lit. Swamishri saw that Thakorji (the murti of God) was facing him. He immediately turned Thakorji 90 degrees, that is, so that the right side of Harikrishna Maharaj was visible to Swamishri!
He said to his attendant, "Thakorji too partakes of the annakut, doesn't he!"
Oh, what subtle, supreme devotion!

st.t: Kids Creations - 233 - Akshardham Forever For Us
w: On October 8, 2023, the whole world rejoiced. This was the day Mahant Swami Maharaj inaugurated Swaminarayan Akshardham in Robbinsville, USA!
Have you explored Akshardham in person or online? If so, we’ve got three questions for you today regarding your experience…

1.What do you like most about Akshardham? Is it the soothing waters of the Brahma Kund? Or the delights that lie in wait in the gift store? Or the Shayona Cafe’s sumptuous treats? Or is it Bhagwan’s majestic murtis? Or something else? Explain your choice.
If you haven’t experienced Akshardham, give it a shot by visiting usa.akshardham.org or ask your parents to stream some videos from our YouTube Channel (@AkshardhamUSA).

My favorite part about Akshardham was Maharaj’s murti, because when you walk in, you instantly see the murti, and his eyes look so loving. Akshardham makes me proud because I can tell my friends about it, and they would enjoy seeing such a magnificent place. Akshardham means to me a place I that I can explain to people about Indian culture and our Sanstha. Sayam Desai (11) Houston, UNITED STATES

1. Oh yeah, that’s easy. The big murti of Sahajanand Swami tilting his head. It looks nice! I like him because he is big and smiling brightly. Also, Gunatitanand Swami is sitting right next to him. 2. Um, because Pramukh Swami Maharaj wanted it there for many people to come visit. 3. It reminds me of Pramukh Swami Maharaj, and one of his last wishes for America. ParamHari Patel (5) Houston, UNITED STATES

1. I like the stained glass behind Sahajanand Swami’s large murti. It has my favorite colors. 2. It makes me proud because no other culture has a structure like Akshardham. 3. There’s no other mandir in North America this large. It made me feel special that I was able to be part of the pratishta as a satsangi. It made me feel that Akshardham is mine, made for me. Swayam Patel (7) Houston, UNITED STATES

I loved walking into Akshardham and seeing all the different murtis of Bhagwan Swaminarayan and his devotees. Growing up America, Akshardham means bringing peace of India to America. Kirtansinh Zala (9) Chino Hills, UNITED STATES

2. One of the things I feel most proud about Akshardham is that so many women helped built it. Most if not none of the women volunteers had absolutely no skills or knowledge about construction but because of their gurus wish, they came, worked hard and successfully accomplished the goal all because of their gurus agna. Akshardham gives me another reason to be proud of being a woman in BAPS! Divya Ronak Patel (12) Los Angeles , UNITED STATES

JAY SWAMINARAYAN 1. I have no words about akshardham but the thing which attracted me the most is the mesmerizing murti of lord swaminarayan it is designed at such an angle that it seems as if he is constantly watching me. I also liked the murti of gunatitanand swami which was filled with dasbhav and divyabhav. Also the tapa murti of nilkanth varni attracted me a lot, his calm and undisturbed pose engaged in deep yoga prayer symbolizes spiritual focus and discipline. All the murtis are an beacon of inspiration. For me it is not only murti but the god himself. 2. Akshardham makes me feel proud proud proud and proud . As it is the largest hindu temple in the united states ! and the 2nd largest hindu temple in the world! which is built by our BAPS sanstha and not only this mandir but the world's largest hindu temple is made by our BAPS sanstha yes! it's delhi akshardham! 3. Akshardham literally means the divine abode of god. It is an eternal place for one to offer devotion and experience everlasting peace. the mandir is a humble tribute to Bhagwan Swaminarayan,the avatars,devas and sages of hinduism. Akshardham inspires me to connect with each other and with Divine. As a child growing in 21st century for me akshardham is not just monument of stones and marbles it is the love and hardwork of our sant's , volunteers and of course our guruhari Mahant Swami Maharaj. all this wouldn't have been possible without the blessings of PSM , lord swaminarayan and our spiritual successor . JAY SWAMINARAYAN ! HITANSHI DHILLON (13) DELHI , INDIA

Jai swaminarayan, something that I like about the akshardham is the murti of Nilkanth Varni, and also I like the murti of Bhagwan Swaminarayan. Something about the Akshardham that I am proud of is that all of the people made this akshardham to make swami proud and also that they took out their own time to help to do the seva for akshardham. Shreena Patel (11) Adelaide, AUSTRALIA

What I love most about Akshardham is the majestic murti of Bhagwan and how it embraces every detail of himself. The fact that Mahant Swami himself added such specific details to the murti, like those on Maharaj's vastra and his overall appearance, is truly inspiring. Mahant Swami Maharaj's attention to detail throughout Akshardham shows how much thought he put into making it perfect.↵ The aspect of Akshardham that fills me with pride is its status as the largest temple outside Asia. It not only symbolizes significant figures from our Sanstha (baps) but also represents Hinduism on a broader scale. Akshardham seamlessly integrates diverse styles, blending traditional and modern elements stunningly. To me, Akshardham gives hope that our culture, not just as a BAPS Satsangi but also as a Hindu, will continue to thrive even when the world around us is falling apart. To me, it means that our culture will endure and flourish in the face of challenges. Aastha (16) Perth, AUSTRALIA
